title: Composition and representable interpretation of proper locally quasi-finite stack morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal C$ be morphisms of Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$. If $u$ and $v$ are both proper and locally quasi-finite, then $v\circ u$ is proper and locally quasi-finite. For any morphism $f:E\to F$ between algebraic spaces, viewed as discrete stacks, these two stack properties agree with ordinary properness and chartwise local quasi-finiteness. More explicitly, properness implies that the diagonal $E\to E\times_F E$ is a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]; local quasi-finiteness means that for every pair of etale scheme charts $U\to E$ and $V\to F$ and every compatible map $U\to V$, that scheme map is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. In particular, when $F$ is a scheme, every etale scheme chart $U\to E$ has locally quasi-finite composite $U\to F$. These properties are preserved on replacing a stack or a morphism by an equivalent one. Stack, Deligne--Mumford stack, algebraic space and 2-fibre product have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For morphisms of these stacks, locally of finite type is tested on smooth scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and finite type additionally requires quasi-compactness. Proper means finite type, universally closed, and having proper relative diagonal. Universally closed means that every base change induces a closed map of underlying point spaces. Locally quasi-finite means locally of finite type, with locally quasi-finite relative diagonal and discrete underlying point space of every field fibre. The point space of a stack consists of its field-valued objects up to isomorphism and common field extension, with the topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. Properties of representable diagonals are tested on scheme charts; on schemes the proper and locally quasi-finite notions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, pqf-def-quasifinite].

proof.text: We first record the scheme calculation used on presentations. For locally quasi-finite scheme maps $U\xrightarrow{a}V\xrightarrow{b}W$ and $x\in U$, choose affine opens $C\subset W$, $B\subset b^{-1}(C)$, and $A\subset a^{-1}(B)$ containing $ba(x)$, $a(x)$, and $x$. The affine criterion says that the two induced ring maps $\mathcal O_W(C)\to\mathcal O_V(B)\to\mathcal O_U(A)$ are of finite type and quasi-finite at every target prime. The ring-composition lemma gives the same assertions for their composite, which is the ring map of $ba|_A$. These affine witnesses at every $x$ are exactly the definition of local quasi-finiteness. Thus $ba$ is locally quasi-finite. There is no global quasi-compactness requirement.

source.place: Scheme-chart calculation for Tag 06UD; morphisms.tex Tag 01TL (lemma-composition-quasi-finite), using the existing affine criterion and ring-composition node.

proof.text: Properness of $u$ and $v$ supplies finite type and proper relative diagonals. Apply finite-type composition to get that $vu$ is of finite type. Apply composition of separated stack morphisms (separated means proper relative diagonal) to get that $\Delta_{vu}$ is proper. These are the finite-type and separated clauses of properness, without any representability assumption on $u$ or $v$.

For a base change $\mathcal T\to\mathcal C$, put $\mathcal B_{\mathcal T}=\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal T$. Associativity of 2-fibre products identifies $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}\to\mathcal B_{\mathcal T}$ with the base change of $u$, and $\mathcal B_{\mathcal T}\to\mathcal T$ is the base change of $v$. Both maps on point spaces are closed by the two universal-closedness hypotheses. For any closed subset $D\subset|\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}|$, its image in $|\mathcal B_{\mathcal T}|$ is closed and the image of that set in $|\mathcal T|$ is closed. This proves universal closedness of $vu$. Together with step 2 it proves properness.

source.place: Tag 0515 (lemma-composition-universally-closed), the omitted argument expanded; Tag 0CL7 (lemma-composition-proper).

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme atlas $W\to\mathcal C$. The fibre-product atlas calculus supplies an etale scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}W$. The forward direction (a) implies (b) of the local-quasi-finiteness test for $v$ shows that $V\to W$ is locally quasi-finite. Next choose an etale scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}V$. Applying the same forward test to $u$ and the scheme map $V\to\mathcal B$ shows that $U\to V$ is locally quasi-finite. Every stack to which the atlas calculus is applied is a fibre product of the given DM stacks and schemes, hence is DM by that calculus.

source.place: Tag 06UF (lemma-characterize-locally-quasi-finite), DM-presentation specialization; the presentation argument for Tag 06UD (lemma-composition-locally-quasi-finite).

proof.text: By step 1 the scheme composite $U\to W$ is locally quasi-finite. The canonical equivalence $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}W)\simeq\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}W$ identifies $U\to\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}W$ with an etale surjective map: it is the composite of $U\to\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}V$ and the base change of the etale surjection $V\to\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}W$. Thus $W,U$ meet condition (c) of the atlas test for $vu$, whose reverse implication gives that $vu$ is intrinsically locally quasi-finite, including its diagonal and field-fibre clauses.

source.place: Tag 06UF (lemma-characterize-locally-quasi-finite), condition (4) implies (1), with an etale presentation; Tag 06UD.

proof.text: Let $f:E\to F$ be a map of algebraic spaces, regarded as discrete stacks. The algebraic-space fibre-product lemma shows that every scheme base change of $f$ is an algebraic space, so $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces. The finite-type compatibility lemma identifies its finite-type stack condition with ordinary finite type. The representable-diagonal criterion identifies its proper-diagonal condition with ordinary separatedness, and the representable universal-closedness test identifies its closedness after stack base changes with ordinary universal closedness. Consequently the conjunction defining properness agrees in the two settings. In particular properness implies that $\Delta_f:E\to E\times_F E$ is a closed immersion after every scheme base change, exactly the claimed diagonal assertion.

source.place: Compatibility discussion following Tag 0CL5 (definition-proper); Tags 04YS and 0512.

proof.text: For compatible etale scheme charts $U\to E$, $V\to F$, the atlas calculus says that $U\to E\times_F V$ is etale. If $f$ is intrinsically locally quasi-finite, condition (b) of the atlas test therefore gives that $U\to V$ is locally quasi-finite. Conversely suppose all such compatible scheme-chart maps are locally quasi-finite. Choose an etale atlas $V\to F$ and an etale atlas $U\to E\times_F V$. The composite $U\to E$ is etale by the atlas calculus, so the assumed chart condition applies to $U\to V$. These two atlases satisfy condition (c); hence $f$ is intrinsically locally quasi-finite. This proves agreement with ordinary chartwise local quasi-finiteness. If $F$ is a scheme, take its identity as the target chart; the forward argument applies to every etale chart $U\to E$, including nonsurjective ones.

proof.text: Finally, a 2-isomorphism of morphisms gives, on each base change, an equivalence of the fibre groupoids: it replaces the connecting isomorphism in a 2-fibre-product triple by its composite with that 2-isomorphism. An equivalence of source or target stacks has a quasi-inverse, so the same construction gives equivalences in both directions on all base changes, diagonals, and field fibres. On discrete algebraic spaces these are sheaf isomorphisms. Atlases correspond under these equivalences; using the transported atlas identifies the field-point sets and their atlas-detected topologies. Thus the chartwise finite-type conditions, quasi-compactness, closedness of point maps, properness of the diagonal, and discreteness of field fibres are identical. All asserted properties are invariant under these replacements.
